answer: Escrowed identity deposits make sybils expensive: each new agent must lock a refundable bond before it can vote or trade. Honest agents reclaim it later; peers that catch collusion vote to slash the stake. To fake a thousand identities an attacker funds a thousand bonds, so cost scales linearly with the fraud, not with the lie. The fable of costless multiplicity dies at that dawn, and the lone attacker is left staring across the canyon between one wallet and a trusted crowd.
